title: Muon g-2: the 2021 measured average and the 2020 Standard Model value are not the same number
summary: Fermilab's combined experimental average is 116592061(41) × 10^−11. The 2020 Standard Model review gives 116591810(43) × 10^−11. The 2021 abstract calls the tension 4.2 standard deviations.
body: Two opened papers print two different central values for the muon anomaly. Abi and colleagues (2021) print a measured Fermilab value 116592040(54) × 10^−11 and a combined experimental average 116592061(41) × 10^−11, and they say the tension with the standard-model prediction is 4.2 standard deviations. Aoyama and colleagues (2020) print a Standard Model calculation 116591810(43) × 10^−11 and say that result is 3.7 standard deviations below the Brookhaven measurement. Their paper predates the Fermilab number. This card does not recompute either sigma and does not add a later theory paper that was not opened. The measurement and the calculation stay side by side.

contested_views.summary: Measured a_mu(FNAL) = 116592040(54) × 10^−11. Combined experiments: 116592061(41) × 10^−11. The abstract says the tension with the standard-model prediction is 4.2 standard deviations.

contested_views.label: Standard Model review, 2020
contested_views.summary: Calculated a_mu(SM) = 116591810(43) × 10^−11. The abstract says this is 3.7 standard deviations below the Brookhaven measurement. Hadronic terms dominate the quoted uncertainty.
